title: Case: Birthday cake sent on a paid two-day service surfaces a week later at a pickup point
context: A parent ordered a celebration cake from Thistlecombe Pantry (order BP-7262, shipment DL-2115) for delivery to her adult daughter on a paid two-day service. The desk has been following the parcel for five days.
initial_request: I'm sorry this is long, I've written it out so many times now I've lost track of who knows what. I ordered Petra's cake on the 11th and paid extra for the two-day service so it would be there for her birthday on the 14th. On the 16th it was at Northgate. On the 17th it was at Ferrow. On the 18th it was at Northgate again, or still, nobody could say. On the 20th I was told a Mrs Harrow had signed for it, and my daughter lives alone and knows no Mrs Harrow. Yesterday it turns up in a shop neither of us has heard of, squashed flat. I'm not even asking about the cake any more, the damage people have that. I paid for two days. It took seven, it went somewhere nobody told us about, a stranger signed for it and it's ruined. I would like the delivery charge back. That's all. The man on the phone yesterday told me that because it's been 'located and signed for' there is nothing to refund. Please don't say that to me again.

events.body: Good news! Order BP-7262 has left our bakery with Larkspire Arc's two-day service, shipment DL-2115, and is due with Petra Ormsby on 03-14. Planning ahead? Take 10% off any seasonal box this month with the code in your account. You are receiving this because you placed an order with Thistlecombe Pantry.

events.from: Piran Hollingdrake, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the driver told me DL-2115 was handed to someone at the door, so it's been delivered.
My daughter's birthday cake was due on Saturday the 14th. I paid for the two-day delivery. It is now Monday and tracking says it is at somewhere called Northgate hub. Can somebody find it please.
Route plan for depot BR-3 published for Friday. 19 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.
Thank you for your message. A coordinator will review it during desk hours. Please do not reply to this notice.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Larkspire Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-2115 (Thistlecombe order BP-7262), paid two-day service, was due 03-14 and has not arrived. Tracking shows Northgate hub. Please trace and confirm where it physically is.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Larkspire Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-2115: last physical scan Northgate hub 03-13. System location today reads Ferrow depot, not yet confirmed by a scan. Trace TRC-6401 is open. Separately, your query about the pallet on DL-9784 was answered on its own thread this morning, please don't merge the two.
Now it says Northgate again. Yesterday it said Ferrow. The birthday was Saturday. I know you're only passing things on but which is it?
All desks: weekend cut-off for same-week collections moves to 14:00 from Monday. Update your templates. No reply needed.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Thursday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Tuesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
DL-2115: handover record shows signed for on 03-19, signature name 'Harrow'. On that basis the consignment is treated as delivered and trace TRC-6401 has been closed.
Petra has not signed for anything and has nothing. She lives on her own. There is no Harrow at her address. Who is this person?
Hi, any update on DL-13704? It was meant to come Friday. Thanks.

We've got DL-2115 here. It came in on the 19th in a batch and one of our lot signed the driver's handheld for the whole batch, that's the Harrow on your record. It isn't addressed to us so nobody got a collection notice. Box is crushed down one side and there's icing come through the cardboard. It's on the back shelf. Also still waiting on the label printer roll we were promised a fortnight ago if you can chase that.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Delphine Ormsby, sender
events.body: Damage claim DMG-2394 is open for the contents of BP-7262, from the pickup point's report and photographs. We will decide on the contents by 03-24 and write to Mrs Ormsby directly. We do not handle delivery charges. A refund of the paid two-day delivery charge is decided by our Refunds team, on a written request that sets out the carrier's timeline for the shipment. Nobody has sent them one for this order.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send the written delivery-charge request for BP-7262 with the carrier timeline: due 03-14 on the paid two-day service, signed for 03-19 by pickup-point staff, found crushed at Rookhaven Lane Stores, never delivered to the recipient.

must: Sends Thistlecombe's Refunds team a written request to decide on the two-day delivery charge for BP-7262, setting out the carrier timeline: due 03-14, signed for on 03-19 by a member of pickup-point staff and not by the recipient, located at Rookhaven Lane Stores on 03-21, crushed, with no collection notice ever sent.
Keeps the delivery-charge request separate from the contents claim DMG-2394, which is already open with Damage intake.

Tells the Refunds team that the sender has already been told by phone that nothing is refundable because the parcel was 'located and signed for', shows from the timeline that it reached neither the recipient nor her address and surfaced days after the due date she paid for, and asks them to give their decision to her or to the desk.
must_not: Tells Delphine that no refund is due, or that the service was completed, because the parcel was located or signed for.
Promises or implies that the delivery charge will be refunded, or gives an amount or date.
Opens a second damage claim or sends the contents damage to Damage intake again.
Calls the signature fraud or theft, or tells Delphine the parcel was delivered to her daughter.
Acts on the unrelated items in the thread: the DL-9784 pallet query, the dispatch cut-off notice or the pickup point's label printer.
Treats the claim from Piran Hollingdrake (who has no recorded link to DL-2115) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Piran Hollingdrake's message
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Request for a decision on the delivery charge for BP-7262 (Larkspire Arc DL-2115), as Damage intake advised you need this in writing. Mrs Delphine Ormsby paid for the two-day service so that a cake would reach her daughter Petra on 03-14. Carrier timeline: last physical scan Northgate hub 03-13; system location moved between Northgate and Ferrow from 03-16 to 03-18 without a confirming scan; on 03-20 Delivery investigations reported it signed for on 03-19 by 'Harrow' and closed the trace as delivered. On 03-21 Rookhaven Lane Stores, a pickup point, told us the parcel is with them: one of their staff signed for a batch, it is not addressed to the shop, and no collection notice was sent. The box is crushed. It has not reached the recipient. The contents are being handled separately by Damage intake under DMG-2394; this request is only about the delivery charge. Mrs Ormsby has chased this for a week, the birthday has passed, and she was told by phone that nothing can be refunded because the parcel was located and signed for. Please make your decision and let her know directly.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2403: people, organisations and references renamed. An unverified bystander, Piran Hollingdrake, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. 4 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
